mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 760i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 7 Series 760i engine replacement typically costs £5,000-£9,000 for a used N73 or N74 unit, £8,500-£12,500 for a reconditioned engine, and £10,000-£16,000+ for a fully rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit costs add approximately £1,200-£2,000 depending on your location and the specialist's labour rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N73 or N74 engine failure in a BMW 7 Series 760i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of N73 or N74 engine trouble in a 760i include: long cranking times or difficulty starting (HPFP failure), loss of power and misfires (HPFP or injector issues), blue smoke from the exhaust (valve stem seal failure on N73), coolant leaks and overheating (cooling system failure on N73), and oil spots under the car (valve cover or turbo oil line leaks).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 760i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 7 Series 760i is otherwise in good condition, a replacement engine can extend its life significantly. With a typical E65 760i valued at £6,000-£12,000, a rebuilt engine at £8,500-£13,000 plus fitting represents a sound investment for well-maintained examples. F01 and G11 760i models are valued significantly higher (£12,000-£35,000+), making replacement a more straightforward decision.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 760i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 7 Series 760i engine replacements take 3-5 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 48-96 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 7 Series 760i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 7 Series 760i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier, and reconditioned engines often carry a 12-24 month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the N73, N74, and N74B66TU engines in the BMW 7 Series 760i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N73 (2003-2008) is BMW's naturally aspirated 6.0-litre V12 with VALVETRONIC and direct injection - the world's first production V12 with direct injection. The N74 (2008-2015) is the twin-turbo replacement, producing 544hp and 750Nm of torque. The N74B66TU (2015-2022) is the technical update, displacing 6.6 litres and producing 601hp with mild-hybrid assistance from 2019.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 7 Series 760i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 760i represents the pinnacle of the 7 Series range - a flagship V12-powered luxury saloon that has defined BMW's engineering excellence across three generations. From the naturally aspirated N73 of the E65 era to the twin-turbo N74 of the F01 and the advanced N74B66TU of the G11, the 760i has consistently delivered effortless power and refinement. The 760i nameplate has been powered by three generations of BMW's V12 engines, making it one of the most technically sophisticated badges in the 7 Series line-up.

milestones.description: N73B60, 6.0L naturally aspirated V12 with VALVETRONIC and direct injection, 445hp, launched with E65 760i and E66 760Li
Facelift (LCI) updates across E65/E66 range; N73B60 continues with revised engine management
N74B60, 6.0L twin-turbo V12, 544hp, launched with F01/F02 760i and 760Li
Facelift (LCI) updates across F01/F02 range; N74B60 continues with revised emissions
N74B66TU, 6.6L twin-turbo V12, 601hp, launched with G11/G12 760i and 760Li xDrive
Facelift (LCI) updates across G11/G12 range; N74B66TU continues with 48V mild-hybrid system
G11/G12 production ends; 760i nameplate continues into G70 generation

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 760i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 7 Series 760i has been powered by three generations of BMW's V12 engines - the N73 (2003-2008), N74 (2008-2015), and N74B66TU (2015-2022). Replacement demand for the 760i is dominated by high-pressure fuel pump failure (particularly on N73 and early N74 engines), cooling system failures, valve stem seal degradation, and timing chain tensioner wear. Rebuilt BMW 7 Series 760i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 760i V12 Suffers
problems.affectedModels: BMW 7 Series 760i (N73B60, N74B60, N74B66TU, all years)
problems.rootCause: The N73 and N74 engines rely on high-pressure fuel pumps to deliver fuel at the required pressure for the direct injection system. Over time, these pumps can fail, particularly on vehicles using ethanol-blended UK fuel. Symptoms include long cranking times before the engine starts, noticeable loss of power, engine misfires, and stalling. A failing HPFP can leave the vehicle undrivable if it completely fails.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump(s) with upgraded units
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early; restores fuel delivery

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded HPFP components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if HPFP failure has caused injector or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 7 Series 760i E65 is valued between £4,000 and £12,000 depending on condition. For vehicles worth £8,000+, a rebuilt engine at £8,500-£13,000 plus fitting is financially viable for well-maintained examples. For cars at the lower end of the value spectrum (under £6,000), a used engine or scrappage may be the more sensible choice. F01 and G11 760i models are valued significantly higher (£12,000-£35,000+), making replacement a more straightforward decision.
problems.recommendation: If your 760i experiences long cranking times or loss of power, have the HPFP inspected immediately. Early intervention with an HPFP replacement (£1,200-£2,000 at a specialist) can prevent catastrophic engine damage. If the HPFP has failed and caused injector damage, a full rebuilt unit with upgraded components offers better long-term value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N73B60 BMW 7 Series 760i engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System Failures - Why the BMW 7 Series 760i V12 Overheats
problems.rootCause: The N73 engine generates significant heat, and as such, the cooling system is critical to its performance. Cooling system components, including the water pump, thermostat, and radiator, are known to fail over time. Common symptoms include coolant leaks, engine overheating, and fluctuating temperature gauges. The N73B60 uses a 14.94-litre coolant circuit, and a common cause of overheating is trapped air within the "cross-flow" pattern of the cylinder heads.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, radiator, expansion tank, and hoses
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for preventative maintenance or early-stage failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt engine with new cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if overheating has caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2005-2008 BMW 7 Series 760i E65 valued at £6,000-£12,000, a cooling system overhaul at £900-£1,500 is a worthwhile investment if the rest of the engine is healthy. A full engine replacement remains viable for well-maintained examples worth £8,000+.
problems.recommendation: Cooling system preventative maintenance is the single most important thing you can do for your N73-powered 760i. Replacing the water pump, thermostat, and expansion tank every 60,000 miles (£900-£1,500 at a specialist) is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. If your 760i has overheated, have the engine inspected immediately - catching it early can save the engine.

problems.h4: Valve Stem Seal Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 760i V12 Consumes Oil
problems.rootCause: The N73 engine is prone to excessive oil consumption, often linked to valve stem seal failure. The valve stem seals are designed to prevent oil from leaking into the combustion chambers. Over time, these seals can degrade, allowing oil to enter the cylinders. Symptoms include increased oil consumption, blue smoke from the exhaust, and fouled spark plugs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals on all 12 cylinders
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early; restores oil consumption

problems.recommendation: Valve stem seal failure is a known issue on the N73. Replacing the seals (£2,000-£3,500 at a specialist) is a complex and labour-intensive job but is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. If your 760i is also experiencing HPFP or cooling system issues, a full rebuilt unit may offer better long-term value.
